seoTitle: How to Put Code Into TradingView (Pine Editor)
metaDescription: Learn how to use the Pine Editor to add custom Pine Script indicators or strategies to TradingView, save your code, and fix common errors.
intro: Getting a custom indicator or strategy running on TradingView starts with correctly using the Pine Editor to paste, save, and apply your Pine Script code. This guide walks through the process step by step and covers fixing the errors that commonly trip up beginners.

steps.heading: Open the Pine Editor
steps.body: From the bottom panel of your TradingView chart, open the Pine Editor to access the code workspace.

steps.heading: Paste your indicator or strategy code
steps.body: Clear the default template and paste your own Pine Script code cleanly into the editor.

steps.heading: Save and add the script to your chart
steps.body: Save the script under a clear name, then use 'Add to chart' to apply the compiled code to your active chart.

steps.heading: Fix common Pine Script errors
steps.body: Watch for version mismatches, missing indicator() or strategy() declarations, and formatting issues introduced by copying from another source.

steps.heading: Understand indicators vs strategies
steps.body: Indicators display visual analysis on the chart, while strategies simulate trade entries and exits for backtesting purposes.

faq.question: Do I need coding experience to use the Pine Editor?
faq.answer: Basic familiarity helps, but many users simply paste existing Pine Script code from tutorials or the community without writing it from scratch.

faq.question: Why does my script show a compile error after pasting?
faq.answer: This is often due to a Pine Script version mismatch or missing declaration line, both of which are fixable by reviewing the top lines of the code.

faq.question: Can I run multiple custom scripts on one chart?
faq.answer: Yes, you can add several indicators to a single chart, though running too many at once may affect performance.

faq.question: Is the Pine Editor available on the free plan?
faq.answer: Yes, the Pine Editor is included in TradingView's free plan, though script limits can vary by subscription tier.
